provider.notes: Aliases are the ones registered at gateway/src/plugin/builtin/mod.rs:1794-1795. The standard factory matches only the exact id 'amivoice' (gateway/src/core/stt/standard.rs:403-405), so a session that uses an alias falls to the flat factory. An empty model becomes -a-general (gateway/src/core/stt/amivoice/config.rs:48, 560-561). The vendor calls models engines; the model id is the engine id, and it fixes the language. Every one of the 20 vendor engines is served on the WebSocket interface, so none needs a segmented path. The important finding is different: the streaming client does not match the vendor protocol (read on both sides, never probed), and no release builds an AmiVoice file transcriber. Today a session still starts and most likely returns nothing. Following integration decisions section 15, the map keeps that client as the transport of every row whose engine it serves, enabled from Release 0 with status known_broken, and reports the defect instead of refusing the session. Repairing the client (one prefix byte and the audio format names) is far less work than a file-upload adapter. Streaming client, as read: The only test runs against an in-repo mock that answers on any binary frame, so it cannot see the missing prefix (gateway/tests/mock_endpoint_e2e.rs:660-704). Whether the client fails against the live service was not tested; both sides were read and no key was available. As written, the client forwards each chunk at once as a binary frame, turns vendor U events into interim results about once a second and turns each vendor A event into a result with is_final and is_speech_final both true (client.rs:557-577; messages.rs:210-213). The vendor's speech-start and speech-end events are only logged (client.rs:545-551). The vendor's own detector ends an utterance after 550 ms of silence by default and force-finalises any utterance at 15 seconds. Other defects found by reading: with the header-format names, 16 kHz raw audio works only through a vendor fallback and any other rate is decoded at the wrong rate; the start command, which contains the API key, is written to the debug log (client.rs:155); a start error containing 'auth' is reported as a bad key although the vendor uses the same message for a wrong engine name (client.rs:203-216); a final with empty text is dropped without reading its error code (client.rs:568-577). The vendor disconnects after 600 seconds without detected speech (the value recorded as the timeout) and after 60 seconds without traffic; a session may last 24 hours. The gateway also accepts short names for engines, for example 'general', 'medical', 'e2e-ja' and 'a2b-multi', and reads every name without regard to case and with underscores as hyphens (gateway/src/core/stt/amivoice/config.rs:275-341). The short names whose engine the client sends unchanged are model_aliases of that engine's row (config.rs:275-341). The lookup compares without case but does not turn underscores into hyphens, so the resolver must do that first. Names the client turns into one of its six non-vendor ids (finance, insurance, finance-input, insurance-input, name-input, address-input and their long forms) are not aliases and land on the default row.

gateway_client.notes: Synchronous request: POST https://acp-api.amivoice.com/v1/recognize (the vendor keeps a log) or https://acp-api.amivoice.com/v1/nolog/recognize (no log; the path also selects the price). Multipart fields u (API key), d (engine id, optionally followed by key=value settings, percent-encoded with %20 for spaces), then the audio part a, which must be last because fields after it are ignored. A WAV header is detected automatically, so the format field c is omitted. The gateway has only unused URL constants for this endpoint (gateway/src/core/stt/amivoice/config.rs:42, 45). The vendor documents a single HTTP 200 response and reports failure in the body's one-character code, so the adapter must classify the body itself: an empty code is success; 'o' means rejected or no speech and is an empty transcript; '+', '-', '%', '^' and 'x' are request or configuration faults that must not be retried ('^' is documented for the asynchronous interface only); 'b', '!', '<', '#', '$', '?' and 'c' may be retried. The code '>' is disputed. The vendor's page lists it with the client errors for which 'retrying will yield the same result' and says it is what an upload without audio data returns; the same page's code table describes it as a failure to send audio inside the vendor's servers; the fact-check lists it as a retry candidate. Retry it at most once, and never for an upload the gateway knows to be empty. The response has no interim text. The vendor runs its own speech detector on the upload, force-finalises a single utterance at 15 seconds and ends the request after 50 seconds without detected speech (the value recorded as the timeout). The vendor's only latency statement for this interface is that conversion finishes 'within 1x the duration of the audio sent, at the latest'; no percentile is published. All processing is in Japan. The vendor's asynchronous job API takes tens of seconds to minutes just to start a job and is not a live transport, so it is not listed.

segment_profile.rationale: Two deviations from the gateway defaults. Maximum segment 14 seconds instead of 25: the synchronous interface force-finalises a single utterance at 15 seconds at an arbitrary point, so the gateway must cut at a pause before that. Request timeout 15 seconds: the vendor's only bound for this interface is 'within 1x the duration of the audio sent', which for a 14 second segment plus padding is about 15 seconds; it is an upper bound from a vendor statement, not a measured figure, and should be replaced by a measured value. Container, 16 kHz rate, pre-roll, trailing silence and two uploads in flight stay at the defaults: silence is not billed and no concurrency limit is published.

billing.notes: Billed per second, and only for the speech the vendor's own detector finds: silence is not charged, on the socket or on upload. The vendor states there is no minimum fee per request. Speech that is detected but then rejected as filler or noise is still billed. Monthly usage is rounded down to whole seconds; there is a monthly floor of 50 yen (no charge below it) and 60 free minutes a month. The price depends on the engine tier and on whether the logging endpoint is used. There is no AmiVoice entry in gateway/src/config/pricing.rs, so no pricing_key is given.

provenance.notes: Hybrid engine, Japanese conversation. Accepts 8 kHz and 16 kHz audio. The vendor serves it on the WebSocket interface and on the synchronous HTTP interface, so it is not file-only and file upload is a fallback. Today's streaming client is known broken, so a session that names this engine very probably gets no transcript until that client is repaired; the map keeps it as the session's transport, enabled from Release 0, and reports the defect rather than refusing the session (integration decisions section 15). The engine id fixes the language. Vocabulary can be extended with a per-request word list or a stored dictionary. This is the gateway's default engine, and also what any unrecognised model string becomes today (gateway/src/core/stt/amivoice/config.rs:48, 560-563). gateway_client.notes: Synchronous request: POST https://acp-api.amivoice.com/v1/recognize (the vendor keeps a log) or https://acp-api.amivoice.com/v1/nolog/recognize (no log; the path also selects the price). Multipart fields u (API key), d (engine id, optionally followed by key=value settings, percent-encoded with %20 for spaces), then the audio part a, which must be last because fields after it are ignored. A WAV header is detected automatically, so the format field c is omitted. The gateway has only unused URL constants for this endpoint (gateway/src/core/stt/amivoice/config.rs:42, 45). The vendor documents a single HTTP 200 response and reports failure in the body's one-character code, so the adapter must classify the body itself: an empty code is success; 'o' means rejected or no speech and is an empty transcript; '+', '-', '%', '^' and 'x' are request or configuration faults that must not be retried ('^' is documented for the asynchronous interface only); 'b', '!', '<', '#', '$', '?' and 'c' may be retried. The code '>' is disputed. The vendor's page lists it with the client errors for which 'retrying will yield the same result' and says it is what an upload without audio data returns; the same page's code table describes it as a failure to send audio inside the vendor's servers; the fact-check lists it as a retry candidate. Retry it at most once, and never for an upload the gateway knows to be empty. The response has no interim text. The vendor runs its own speech detector on the upload, force-finalises a single utterance at 15 seconds and ends the request after 50 seconds without detected speech (the value recorded as the timeout). The vendor's only latency statement for this interface is that conversion finishes 'within 1x the duration of the audio sent, at the latest'; no percentile is published. All processing is in Japan. The vendor's asynchronous job API takes tens of seconds to minutes just to start a job and is not a live transport, so it is not listed.

segment_profile.rationale: Two deviations from the gateway defaults. Maximum segment 14 seconds instead of 25: the synchronous interface force-finalises a single utterance at 15 seconds at an arbitrary point, so the gateway must cut at a pause before that. Request timeout 15 seconds: the vendor's only bound for this interface is 'within 1x the duration of the audio sent', which for a 14 second segment plus padding is about 15 seconds; it is an upper bound from a vendor statement, not a measured figure, and should be replaced by a measured value. Container, 16 kHz rate, pre-roll, trailing silence and two uploads in flight stay at the defaults: silence is not billed and no concurrency limit is published.

gateway_client.notes: The only test runs against an in-repo mock that answers on any binary frame, so it cannot see the missing prefix (gateway/tests/mock_endpoint_e2e.rs:660-704). Whether the client fails against the live service was not tested; both sides were read and no key was available. As written, the client forwards each chunk at once as a binary frame, turns vendor U events into interim results about once a second and turns each vendor A event into a result with is_final and is_speech_final both true (client.rs:557-577; messages.rs:210-213). The vendor's speech-start and speech-end events are only logged (client.rs:545-551). The vendor's own detector ends an utterance after 550 ms of silence by default and force-finalises any utterance at 15 seconds. Other defects found by reading: with the header-format names, 16 kHz raw audio works only through a vendor fallback and any other rate is decoded at the wrong rate; the start command, which contains the API key, is written to the debug log (client.rs:155); a start error containing 'auth' is reported as a bad key although the vendor uses the same message for a wrong engine name (client.rs:203-216); a final with empty text is dropped without reading its error code (client.rs:568-577). The vendor disconnects after 600 seconds without detected speech (the value recorded as the timeout) and after 60 seconds without traffic; a session may last 24 hours.
gateway_client.defect: Known broken: the client does not match the vendor's wire protocol. Audio frames and the keep-alive frame are sent without the mandatory first byte 0x70 ('p') (gateway/src/core/stt/amivoice/client.rs:266-268, 335-336), and raw PCM is declared with the format names 8K and 16K, which the vendor reserves for audio that has a file header (gateway/src/core/stt/amivoice/config.rs:403-404, 419-425). Treat it as working only after both are fixed and one live call has returned a transcript.

billing.notes: Billed per second, and only for the speech the vendor's own detector finds: silence is not charged, on the socket or on upload. The vendor states there is no minimum fee per request. Speech that is detected but then rejected as filler or noise is still billed. Monthly usage is rounded down to whole seconds; there is a monthly floor of 50 yen (no charge below it) and 60 free minutes a month. The price depends on the engine tier and on whether the logging endpoint is used. There is no AmiVoice entry in gateway/src/config/pricing.rs, so no pricing_key is given.

provenance.notes: Default for an AmiVoice engine id the map has never seen. Every engine the vendor offers streams, but the gateway's streaming client does not match the vendor protocol. File upload is listed first, where the builders placed it as the path a wrong guess can survive, but no release builds an AmiVoice file transcriber, so that transport is never enabled and such a session gets the streaming client, known broken, reported and not refused. The resolver must attach a warning that the capability was assumed. Six ids that the gateway itself accepts are not in the vendor's engine table and land on this row: -a-finance, -a-insurance, -a-finance-input, -a-insurance-input, -a-name-input and -a-address-input (gateway/src/core/stt/amivoice/config.rs:116-161). They have no row because the map has no way to mark an id as known to be invalid; the code must replace them with the vendor ids. Today the client turns any unrecognised string into -a-general without warning (config.rs:563); the provider's native_model_handling (substituted) makes the resolver warn with stt_model_substituted instead.
